answer: Anchor each agent identity to an escrowed stake that is slashed when a fake identity is exposed: forging a crowd then costs real capital per sock-puppet, like filling a canyon one stone at a time, while honest agents accumulate a lantern of peer attestations that makes their history cheap to verify. An attacker must pay the stake for every fake and lose it on detection, so the cost of manufacturing identities exceeds any gain from gaming the market.
